_doc: ONE FIXTURE, TWO SUITES — the server's blend and the browser's twin must draw the same line.
Read by `fundamentalBlend.parity.test.ts` (vitest) and `backend/tests/test_blend_client_parity.py`
(pytest). It lives HERE, under the frontend, because vite refuses to serve a file outside its
root while python can read anything — so the only workable direction is python reaching across.
The case it encodes: an index whose payload lists a constituent the LINE was never handed. The
chart is blended over `_members(universe, require_market_cap=True)`; the drill-down payload is
`all_constituents=True`, which keeps the constituents with no stored market cap at weight 0 so
the table can say 'in the index, not in the line'. `Echo` is one of those. It can never carry a
weight, so it is out of every average on both sides — but until 2026-09-03 it still counted in
the CLIENT's names-coverage denominator (`parts.length`), where the server's `total_n` never
saw it. 2016 and 2017 are built to sit EXACTLY on the 50% floor: two of the four weighted
members report them.
client before the fix   2/5 = 40.0%  -> refused -> 100, ..., 126.475 at 2018
The gap is not a missing point: skipping a period makes the next step span two intervals, so
every level after it is a product over a different partition. Echo's own series runs 100 -> 800
so that a leak into the line would be unmissable rather than a rounding difference.
⚠ THE VALUES ARE THE FIXTURE AND THE EXPECTED SERIES IS DERIVED FROM THEM BY HAND, not captured
from either implementation. A baseline captured from one side would pin that side's bugs as the
contract; both suites are supposed to be checkable against the arithmetic below.
weights are equal (caps all 100), so each step is a plain mean of the members' growth:
Charlie/Delta are carried into 2016 (one period) and dropped by 2017 (two), so they
span the first step at g=0 and neither of the last two.
metric_code: annuals__Per Share Data__Month End Stock Price
